items.originalTitle: 'Now we need to go further' - Hamilton outlines next targets to improve F1 diversity
items.summaryEn: Lewis Hamilton says Formula 1 has shown over the past five years that change is possible and that the sport now needs to go further in creating opportunities for the next generation. His Mission 44 foundation released a new report titled 'Igniting Inclusion' with three recommendations to help more young people from under-represented backgrounds get into and stay in F1.
detailZh: 刘易斯·汉密尔顿表示，改善F1多元化的工作“远未完成”，Mission 44基金会同时提出了进一步变革的建议。
这位七届世界冠军的Mission 44基金会提出三项建议，帮助更多来自代表性不足背景的年轻人进入并留在F1；汉密尔顿对2021年以来这项运动出现的变化感到“鼓舞”，并“为我们的成就感到自豪”，同时认为还可以做得更多。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿表示，F1在过去五年“已证明改变是可能的”，如今在增加下一代机会方面“需要更进一步”。
汉密尔顿委员会提出变革建议五年后，这位七届世界冠军的Mission 44基金会发布了一份题为《点燃包容》的新报告，回顾了黑人、女性以及来自低收入背景的年轻人的进展。
报告承认了自2021年以来这项运动取得的“重大进步”，其中包括签署多元与包容宪章——全部11支车队、F1和FIA均为签署方——设立工程奖学金以及推出F1学院。这项运动上月还发布了首份社会影响报告。

汉密尔顿对这些成就表示欢迎，同时也觉得“仍有许多事情要做”。
“我想首先说声谢谢。感谢各车队、一级方程式（F1）以及国际汽联（FIA），他们签署了这项运动历史上第一份多元与包容宪章，”这位法拉利车手在报告中说道。
“感谢车队内部那些设立了2021年尚不存在的奖学金、实习岗位和导师计划的人们。感谢每周将这项运动带入课堂的教师、慈善机构和志愿者们。
“如今当我走过围场时，我看到的女性更多了，黑人和棕色人种的面孔更多了，看起来像看台上车迷的人比我从开始职业生涯以来的任何时候都多。
这令人振奋，推动此事的人们值得称赞。然而，仍有许多工作要做。
“我们已经打开了大门，但还没有学会统计有多少人走进来，又有多少人留下来。”
“这项运动的首份社会影响报告展示了正在发生的诸多事情。这份报告要问的是，这一切加起来意味着什么。这是一项以千分之一秒衡量表现的运动。我们也可以衡量这一点。”
早在2023年，刘易斯·汉密尔顿就解释了他的使命：在赛车运动领域改变来自服务不足社区的年轻人的生活。
Mission 44 的报告提出了三项建议。
第一项是每年公布一份覆盖整个赛车运动的图景，按性别、族裔和社会经济背景说明谁加入、谁晋升、谁离开。
第二项，报告呼吁将人才投资——首先是学徒薪资——排除在赛车运动的预算帽之外，并且 F1、国际汽联、各车队和商业合作伙伴随后“在未来五年内投入至少 5000 万英镑的新资金，帮助来自代表性不足背景的年轻人进入赛车运动职业，并支持他们留下来”。
第三项建议是，每支车队都应承诺“每年公布一定数量的带薪、可及的职业生涯早期岗位，到 2030 年建成数千条进入赛车运动的带薪通道”，同时“对自动化筛选进行偏见测试并披露其使用情况”。
汉密尔顿补充道：“所以这就是我的请求。致每一位车队领队、每一位首席执行官，以及一级方程式和FIA的领导者们：让我们把这份报告中的三项建议付诸实施。”
F1上个月发布了其首份全运动社会影响报告。
报告显示，2025年，来自71个国家的超过50万年轻人参与并受益于一级方程式在教育和社区外展方面的项目，同时超过2500名年轻人在F1赛道参加了活动。
报告还宣布将其工程奖学金延长三年，至少持续到2028/29学年，并承诺再提供240万英镑的资金。
该报道还补充称，这项运动将“加强其在治理、衡量和报告方面的方法，以更好地理解成果、分享进展，并最大化其社会影响工作的长期价值”。
一位F1发言人表示：“我们为那些有助于激励下一代一级方程式车手和参与者的项目和倡议感到自豪，也为它们如何持续增加我们这项运动中的参与机会和可及性感到自豪。
“在汉密尔顿委员会提出建议之后，这项运动于2024年签署了其有史以来第一份多元与包容（D&I）宪章，并在2025年首次开展了全运动范围的数据收集工作，以了解我们社会影响项目的全球覆盖情况。
“这表明，仅在2025赛季，全球就有超过50万名年轻人参与了教育、STEM和激励项目，并且我们这项运动中提供了超过1000个结构化的技能和人才发展机会。
“随着一级方程式赛车在全球舞台上的持续发展，我们深化和演进社会影响力的雄心也在不断增强。我们与F1各车队、国际汽联以及这项运动的广大成员一道，致力于在这一基础上继续建设，并期待分享我们下一阶段的工作。”
在表达对未来取得更多进展的希望时，汉密尔顿表示：“从工程奖学金和多元与包容宪章，到激励超过50万名年轻人，我们帮助推动了真正的进展。我为我们所取得的成就感到自豪，但我们远未完成。”
“一级方程式赛车正在激励全世界数百万年轻人。但如果没有机会，激励就毫无意义。我们不能告诉年轻人要胸怀大志，然后当他们试图将这些梦想变为现实时却不打开大门。”
“F1、国际汽联和每支车队都必须加大力度、加快步伐。我们需要真正的投资、更多的机会和更强的问责制。我们已经证明改变是可能的。现在我们需要走得更远。人才就在那里，而我们这项运动的未来取决于能否释放他们的潜力。”

detailEn: Lewis Hamilton says work improving diversity in F1 'nowhere near finished' as Mission 44 outlines recommendations for further change

The seven-time champion's Mission 44 foundation outlines three recommendations to help more young people from under-represented backgrounds get into and stay in F1; Hamilton "heartened" by changes seen in the sport since 2021 and "proud of what we've achieved" and believes more can be done

Lewis Hamilton says Formula 1 has "shown that change is possible" to improve diversity in the sport over the past five years and "now we need to go further" in increasing opportunities for the next generation.

Five years after the Hamilton Commission made its recommendations for change, the seven-time world champion's Mission 44 foundation released a new report titled 'Igniting Inclusion' reviewing progress for Black people, women and young people from lower-income backgrounds.

The report acknowledged the "significant steps forward" made in the sport since 2021, which include the signing of a diversity and inclusion charter - which all 11 teams, F1 and the FIA are signatories to - the creation of an engineering scholarship and the launch of F1 Academy. The sport also published its first social impact report last month.

Hamilton welcomed those achievements and also feels "there is much still to do".

"I want to start by saying thank you. To the teams, to Formula 1 and to the FIA, who signed the first Diversity and Inclusion Charter in the history of this sport," said the Ferrari driver in the report.

"To the people inside the teams who built scholarships, placements and mentoring schemes that did not exist in 2021. To the teachers, charities and volunteers who take the sport into classrooms every week.
"When I walk through the paddock now, I see more women, more Black and Brown faces, more people who look like the fans in the grandstands than at any point since I started.
"That is heartening, and the people behind it deserve credit. And yet, there is much still to do.
"We have opened the door, but we have not yet learned to count how many people walk through it, or how many stay.

"The sport's first Social Impact Report shows how much is happening. This report asks what it adds up to. This is a sport that measures performance to the thousandth of a second. We can measure this too."
Back in 2023, Lewis Hamilton explained his mission to transform the lives of young people from underserved communities in the world of motorsport
Mission 44's report makes three recommendations.
The first is for the publication of one sport-wide picture each year of who joins, who is promoted and who leaves, by gender, ethnicity and socio-economic background.

Secondly, the report calls for talent investment, starting with apprentice salaries, to be excluded from the sport's budget cap and that F1, the FIA, the teams and commercial partners then "invest at least £50m of new money over the next five years in helping young people from under-represented backgrounds into motorsport careers, and supporting them to stay".

The third recommendation is for every team to commit to "a published number of paid, accessible early-career places each year, building thousands of paid routes into motorsport by 2030", while "automated screening is tested for bias and its use disclosed".
Hamilton added: "So here is what I am asking. To every team principal, every chief executive and the leaders of Formula 1 and the FIA: let's make the three recommendations in this report happen."
F1 last month published its first sport-wide social impact report.

It showed that more than 500,000 young people across 71 countries accessed and benefitted from Formula 1 programmes in education and community outreach in 2025, while over 2,500 young people took part in activities at F1 race tracks.
It also announced a three-year extension to its engineering scholarship until at least 2028/29, committing to a further £2.4m in funding.

That report added the sport will "strengthen its approach to governance, measurement and reporting to better understand results, share progress and maximise the long-term value of its social impact work".
An F1 spokesperson said: "We are proud of the programmes and initiatives which help inspire the next generation of Formula 1 and how they continue to increase access and opportunity across our sport.

"Following recommendations from the Hamilton Commission, the sport signed its first ever D&I charter in 2024, and in 2025, conducted its first ever sport wide data gathering exercise to capture the global reach of our social impact programmes.

"This showed that in the 2025 season alone, more than 500,000 young people engaged in education, STEM and inspiration programmes globally and over 1,000 structured skills and talent development opportunities across our sport.

"As Formula 1 continues to grow on the global stage, so too does our ambition to deepen and evolve our social impact. We are committed, alongside the F1 teams, the FIA and broader members of our sport to continue building on this foundation and look forward to sharing the next phase of our work."

Expressing his hopes for more progress in future, Hamilton said: "From engineering scholarships and the Diversity and Inclusion Charter to inspiring over 500,000 young people, we've helped drive real progress. I'm proud of what we've achieved, but we're nowhere near finished.

"Formula 1 is inspiring millions of young people around the world. But inspiration means nothing without opportunity. We can't tell young people to dream big and then not open the doors when they try to make those dreams a reality.

"F1, the FIA and every team must push harder and move faster. We need real investment, more opportunities and greater accountability. We've shown that change is possible. Now we need to go further. The talent is out there, and the future of our sport depends on unlocking it."

据《每日邮报》报道，七届F1世界冠军刘易斯·汉密尔顿希望在洛杉矶安家，以便在冬歇期有更多时间陪伴伴侣金·卡戴珊及其孩子。
报道称，这位法拉利车手曾就马里布、太平洋帕利塞德和好莱坞山的房产与房产中介接触，并正在权衡是租还是买。他的主要住所位于摩纳哥，而卡戴珊住在隐山，那是洛杉矶市中心西北部的一个封闭式社区。
两人自一月起被传出恋情，汉密尔顿后来在社交媒体上分享了他们的合照。此后卡戴珊成为维修区的熟悉面孔，六月在摩纳哥、上个月在新加坡观看他比赛。
汉密尔顿也温情地谈到她与说唱歌手坎耶·韦斯特婚姻所生的孩子诺斯、圣、普萨姆和芝加哥。
在上个月美国大奖赛前于奥斯汀举行的一场车迷活动上，他说：“我女朋友的孩子们，我很喜欢和他们相处。”
“她有四个孩子，所以我能和这些孩子们一起玩。今年我给他们买了一只狗，所以小Halo是这个家庭的新成员。”
这发生在汉密尔顿起伏不定的赛季之中。在马拉内罗车队经历艰难的第一年后，随着规则的变化，他恢复了昔日夺冠的状态。他在中国大奖赛上为法拉利首次登上领奖台，随后在巴塞罗那庆祝了他身穿红色赛车服的首个大奖赛胜利。
尽管汉密尔顿仍在争夺车手锦标赛第二名，但动力单元罚退以及与队友夏尔·勒克莱尔的赛道冲突影响了最近几场比赛。
本赛季还剩三场比赛，汉密尔顿以261分排名第四，落后第三名梅赛德斯的乔治·拉塞尔一分，落后第二名红牛的马克斯·维斯塔潘18分。基米·安东内利已在墨西哥大奖赛上锁定了车手冠军。
detailEn: Lewis Hamilon reportedly house-hunting in LA amid Kim Kardashian relationship

Seven-time Formula 1 champion Lewis Hamilton wants a Los Angeles base so he can spend more of the winter break with his partner Kim Kardashian and her children, according to a report from the Daily Mail.

The report says the Ferrari driver approached estate agents about houses in Malibu, Pacific Palisades and the Hollywood Hills, and is weighing up whether to rent or buy. His main home is in Monaco, while Kardashian lives in Hidden Hills, a gated community north-west of central Los Angeles.

The couple have been linked since January, and Hamilton later shared photos of them together on social media. Kardashian has since become a familiar face in the paddock, watching him race in Monaco in June and in Singapore last month.
Hamilton has also spoken warmly about her children, North, Saint, Psalm and Chicago, from her marriage to rapper Kanye West.
At a fan event in Austin before last month's United States Grand Prix, he said: "My girlfriend's kids, I love spending time with them.
"She’s got four, so I’m getting to play with these kids. I got them a dog this year, so little Halo is a new member of that family."

This comes amid an up-and-down season for Hamilton. After a rocky first year with the Maranello outfit, he bounced back to his old race-winning form with the turn of the regulations. He secured his first podium with Ferrari at the Chinese Grand Prix and later celebrated his first grand prix win in red in Barcelona.
While Hamilton remains in the fight for second in the drivers' championship, power unit penalties and on-track clashes with his team-mate Charles Leclerc have marred the last few races.

With three races remaining in the season, Hamilton is fourth with 261 points, one point behind Mercedes' George Russell in third and 18 points behind Red Bull's Max Verstappen in second. Kimi Antonelli already secured the drivers' title at the Mexican Grand Prix.

detailZh: F1车手经纪人恩里科·扎纳里尼回顾赛车生涯五十年
恩里科·扎纳里尼回顾了自己与埃迪·埃尔文、亚历山德罗·扎纳尔迪和拉斐尔·卡马拉等人共事的半个世纪——处理人际关系、面对失望，以及一个发生了深刻变化的围场。这么多年过去，他仍然坚信一件事：即使在今天的F1，经验也是不可替代的资产。
有时，一个单一事件——仅仅几秒钟——就足以改变职业生涯的走向。恩里科·扎纳里尼回忆起这样一个时刻，它发生在1993年葡萄牙大奖赛的围场里。埃马努埃莱·纳斯佩蒂是扎纳里尼在20世纪90年代初管理的车手之一，当时正努力保住自己的F1未来。
目标是跑赢队友鲁本斯·巴里切罗——这样的成绩本可以增加他的机会。但在排位赛的决定性时刻，正当纳斯佩蒂全力冲击那可能改变他命运的一圈时，他发现刚出维修区的艾尔顿·塞纳正挡在身前。这次尝试被毁了，正如扎纳里尼所记得的那样，一个重大机会也随之消失。
“这是我们最后的机会，”扎纳里尼告诉Motorsport.com。“埃马努埃莱只剩最后一套轮胎，他必须全力以赴。当我看到塞纳从维修区驶出，而纳斯佩蒂正好到达最后一个弯角时，我就知道我们的圈速毁了。事实正是如此。”
恩里科·扎纳里尼与安东尼奥·吉奥维纳兹，哈斯F1车队
“我告诉自己，不能就这样结束，”他说。“我们必须再试一次——而且要做得更好。这成了我的座右铭之一，成了我生活和工作的原则之一。”
50年过去了，扎纳里尼依然活跃在围场之中。他跨越了不同的时代，认识了几代车手，与冠军和前途无量的年轻才俊都合作过。他的职业生涯始于1975年，当时他管理着一辆Autodelta赛车和两名车手。如今，他与弗朗切斯科·普林奇佩一起，代理的车手包括拉斐尔·卡马拉——后者刚刚代表哈斯完成F1首秀。
在这之间，是一生在赛车运动中度过的时光，而其中最鲜明的特点，是一种独特的经纪人工作方式。“在我们的世界里，你每一天都与车手朝夕相处，”他解释道，“你们会建立起非常紧密的纽带。和埃马努埃莱·纳斯佩蒂，我们就像兄弟一样——对他来说，我或许几乎像第二个父亲。而这些关系并不一定随着赛车生涯的结束而终止。”
最耐人寻味的例子是埃迪·欧文，他是在扎纳里尼职业道路上留下最深印记的车手之一：“埃迪真是把我折腾得够呛。他的情绪起伏极大，尤其是在私生活方面。但我们仍然是朋友。三十年过去了，如今——在巴西和拉斯维加斯之间——我们正一起在秘鲁度假一周。两个老家伙在度假！”
这是一种似乎属于另一个时代的经纪理念，但扎纳里尼仍然认为它至关重要——尤其是因为，在他看来，车手随着时间推移的变化，远没有人们想象的那么大。
他评价道：“纳斯佩蒂、欧文或扎纳尔迪所拥有的那种竞争力，我在今天的卡马拉身上同样能看到。一旦护目镜放下，他们都会变成充满竞争本能的猛兽。”
“最大的变化在于技术和社交媒体的影响。过去，与公众的关系完全不同。如今，年轻车手会花大量时间在手机上——了解信息、直接与人交流。但竞争精神始终如一。”
经验的价值以及与法拉利的关系
几十年来，经纪人的角色也经历了深刻变化。车队和制造商设立青训车队的做法改变了平衡，在某些情况下缩小了车手代表们的施展空间。
“在红牛——至少只要赫尔穆特·马尔科还在掌权——几乎不可能进行任何有意义的对话。他们甚至不会考虑你，除非你恰好是马克斯·维斯塔潘的经纪人。梅赛德斯也采取非常专断的方式，倾向于把经纪人晾在一边。相比之下，法拉利一直尊重我们的工作。哈斯和迈凯伦也是如此。”
与马拉内罗的关系是该经纪公司的一大优势。这段合作始于欧文时代，并延续至今，目前扎纳里尼的公司代理着五名与法拉利有关联的车手。这也是卡马拉将职业生涯托付给该公司的原因。
“拉斐尔来找我们，是因为他想要那种与法拉利建立长期关系所带来的经验，”扎纳里尼解释道。“我们早就认识他，也一直饶有兴趣地关注他的进展，但我们没有主动追求他，因为他当时有另一位经纪人。这是职业道德问题；我们尊重他人的工作。”
道德这个话题在扎纳里尼的叙述中反复出现。“这是一个很容易搞暗箱操作的环境——你可以通过违规操作快速赚钱，”他补充道。“我一直告诉我的团队要行为端正，按规矩办事。这也是你如何长期维持关系的方式。”
扎纳里尼认为，经验是管理者能给予年轻车手的最宝贵财富：“你不必是天才。当你在赛车运动里摸爬滚打50年，你见过太多场景，它们迟早会重演。20年前发生的事，明天早上就可能同样发生在拉斐尔身上。我能让他做好准备，告诉他该期待什么。而且他是个聪明的年轻人，非常尊重经验。”
“在拉斐尔这件事上，我们与巴西一家商业伙伴——FWD经纪公司——的联系也起了关键作用；他们在卡马拉项目上做得非常出色。一切完美地衔接上了。”
为卡马拉在巴西大奖赛完成F1首秀做准备，需要一套特定的方法。在职业生涯一直追逐杆位、分站胜利和年度冠军之后，这位新秀突然发现自己身处一个成功标准完全不同的环境。
“过去一周，我们不得不把一切推倒重来，”扎纳里尼解释道。“我们所在的这支车队——除非出现某些非同寻常的变故——不会去争夺杆位或分站胜利。拉斐尔习惯了为胜利而战，所以我们必须向他解释，如今工作的性质不同了。如果他做得好，总有一天他会拥有一辆能够拿下杆位和胜利的赛车。”
恩里科·扎纳里尼与吉安卡洛·费斯切拉
对扎纳里尼而言，进入F1并不仅仅是一段旅程的顶点，而是一个新篇章的开始。当被问及他管理过的车手中，谁在纯粹天赋上与卡马拉最相似时，他的回答很能说明问题：“也许是[吉安卡洛]费斯切拉。很难做比较，但就纯粹天赋而言，他是第一个浮现在我脑海里的。不过他们的性格完全不同——一个内向，一个外向。”
经理人工作中还有一个很少被关注的方面：管理车手的家庭。“我们实际上已经拿到了‘家长管理’的学位！”扎纳里尼感叹道，“我觉得我们应该得一个特别奖。有时候，管理父母比管理车手更费心。家庭为了帮助孩子达到这些水平牺牲了很多，情感纽带非常牢固。但到了某个阶段，年轻车手需要变得独立，引导这一转变并不总是容易的。”
从罗恩·丹尼斯到扎克·布朗，一个不那么傲慢的围场
扎纳里尼经历过一种F1，在那个世界里，决定由车队老板直接做出——个人关系往往具有决定性，尽管并不总是那么简单直接。
他回忆起与罗恩·丹尼斯的一次会面，那次会面是为了在吉安卡洛·费斯切拉赢得2003年巴西大奖赛后讨论他：“他在伊莫拉附近的酒店房间里接待了我。他从一开始就很傲慢。他告诉我他对费斯切拉不感兴趣，他之所以同意见我，只是因为是我提出的请求。告诉别人你不感兴趣有不同的方式，而他显然没有选择最优雅的那种……”
与迈凯伦现任领导层的对比十分鲜明：“扎克·布朗的精神与我很相似。我总是说我是个二手车销售员，因为我来自那个行业。而当你在展厅工作时，你会学到必须倾听每一个人。可能走进来一个看起来身无分文的人，最后却买了三辆梅赛德斯。扎克倾听每一个人，然后，自然而然地，他得出自己的结论。”
矛盾的是，尽管F1变得复杂和富裕得多，如今在扎纳里尼看来，它却不像过去那样傲慢了：“那时候，有个人所有者；今天，结构不同了，对话也更多了。我在今天的围场里看不到当年我有时会遇到的那种傲慢。”
扎纳里尼对伯尼·埃克莱斯顿时代与自由媒体时代的比较同样不带怀旧情绪。他承认旧体系在当时行之有效，但认为当前的管理层更适合F1如今达到的规模。
安东尼奥·吉奥维纳齐、哈斯F1车队和恩里科·扎纳里尼
从业50年后，扎纳里尼毫无放慢脚步的迹象。当被问及是否曾考虑离开赛车运动时，他立刻回答：“没有——因为第二天我就会死！”
然而，他也意识到经纪公司的未来最终必须托付给新一代。弗朗切斯科·普林奇佩正是在此背景下登场，他被赋予了负责卡马拉项目的职责。
“这个项目完全掌握在他手中，这让我感到无比欣慰，”扎纳里尼说道。“弗朗切斯科·普林奇佩在某种意义上是我自己的创造——我自豪地这么说。我们形成了一种共生关系，他新鲜、年轻的心态与我的经验相辅相成。”
这种纽带超越了职业层面：“我自己的孩子选择了不同的职业道路。在赛车运动的世界里，弗朗切斯科就是我的儿子。我知道我自己的旅程终有一天会结束，但知道会有人将这项工作传承下去，这让我感到欣慰。”
或许这段话最能概括恩里科·扎纳里尼的故事——一个见证了赛车、车队、规则以及赛车运动商业运作方式演变的人。他认识那些后来赢得世界冠军的车手，也认识那些在排位赛刚跑出几米就梦想破灭的人。
而半个世纪后的今天，他依然在那两个曾出现在电视屏幕上的词中看到自己的影子——那是一个格外苦涩的下午：“再努力些。”再试一次——并且做得更好。
detailEn: F1 driver manager Enrico Zanarini recounts his 50 years in motorsport

Enrico Zanarini reflects on half a century spent working alongside the likes of Eddie Irvine, Alessandro Zanardi and Rafael Camara – navigating personal relationships, disappointments, and a profoundly transformed paddock. After all this time, he remains convinced of one thing: experience is an irreplaceable asset, even in today’s F1

Sometimes, a single incident – mere seconds – is enough to alter the course of a career. Enrico Zanarini recalls one such moment, which took place in the paddock at the 1993 Portuguese Grand Prix. Emanuele Naspetti, one of the drivers Zanarini managed in the early 1990s, was striving to secure his Formula 1 future.

The goal was to outperform his team-mate, Rubens Barrichello – a result that could have bolstered his chances. But at the decisive moment during qualifying, just as Naspetti was pushing for the lap that might have changed his destiny, he found Ayrton Senna – who had just exited the pits – directly in his path. The attempt was ruined, and with it, as Zanarini remembers, a major opportunity vanished.

“It was our last chance,” Zanarini told Motorsport.com. “Emanuele had one final set of tires left, and he absolutely had to deliver. When I saw Senna pulling out of the pits just as Naspetti was reaching the final corner, I knew our lap was ruined. And that is exactly what happened.”

Zanarini returned to the paddock, devastated. He absent-mindedly sat down in front of a television, before noticing a Nike commercial. He didn’t pay much attention to the visuals, but the words that appeared at the end stayed with him: “Try Harder” – raise the bar.
Enrico Zanarini and Antonio Giovinazzi, Haas F1 Team
“I told myself it couldn’t end like this,” he said. “We had to give it another try – and do it better. That became one of my mottos, one of the principles by which I live and work.”

After 50 years, Zanarini is still in the paddock. He has spanned different eras, known generations of drivers, and worked with both champions and promising young talents. His career began in 1975, when he managed an Autodelta car and two drivers. Today, alongside Francesco Principe, he represents – among others – Rafael Camara, who has just made his F1 debut with Haas.

In between lies a lifetime spent in motorsport, defined above all by a unique approach to the manager job. “In our world, you live alongside the drivers every single day,” he explained. “You form very close bonds. With Emanuele Naspetti, we were like brothers – to him, I was perhaps almost a second father. And these are relationships that don’t necessarily end when a racing career does.”

The most intriguing example is Eddie Irvine, one of the drivers who left the deepest marks on Zanarini’s professional journey: “Eddie really put me through the wringer. He had incredible mood swings, especially when it came to his private life. Yet, we’re still friends. Thirty years have passed, and now – between Brazil and Las Vegas – we’re vacationing together in Peru for a week. Two old guys on holiday!”

It is a philosophy of management that seems to belong to another era, yet Zanarini still considers it essential – not least because, in his view, drivers have changed far less over time than one might imagine.
“The competitiveness that Naspetti, Irvine, or Zanardi possessed is the same I see in Camara today,” he reckoned. “Once the visor goes down, they all turn into competitive animals.

“What has changed, above all, is the influence of technology and social media. In the past, the relationship with the public was completely different. Today, a young driver spends a lot of time on his phone – staying informed, communicating directly with people. But the competitive spirit remains the same.”
The value of experience and the relationship with Ferrari

Over the decades, the role of a manager has also undergone profound change. The emergence of academies run by teams and manufacturers has shifted the balance, in some cases narrowing the scope for those who represent the drivers.

“With Red Bull – at least as long as Helmut Marko was in charge – it was practically impossible to engage in any meaningful dialogue. They wouldn’t even consider you, unless you happened to be Max Verstappen’s manager. Mercedes also takes a very authoritarian approach, tending to keep managers on the sidelines. Ferrari, by contrast, has always respected our work. The same can be said for Haas and McLaren.”

The relationship with Maranello is one of the agency’s key strengths. It is a partnership that began back in the Irvine days and lives on, with five Ferrari-linked drivers currently represented by Zanarini’s organisation. This was also why Camara trusted the agency with his career.

“Rafael came to us because he was looking for the experience that comes with an established relationship with Ferrari,” Zanarini explained. “We already knew him and had been following his progress with interest, but we didn’t actively pursue him because he had another manager. It’s a matter of professional ethics; we respect the work of others.”

The subject of ethics comes up repeatedly in Zanarini’s account. “This is an environment where it’s easy to engage in underhanded practices – where you could make quick money by operating outside the rules,” he added. “I’ve always told my team to conduct themselves properly and to do things the right way. That is also how you maintain relationships over time.”

According to Zanarini, experience is the greatest asset a manager can offer a young driver: “You don’t have to be a genius. When you’ve spent 50 years in motorsport, you’ve seen so many scenarios that, sooner or later, are bound to repeat themselves. Something that happened 20 years ago could just as easily happen to Rafael tomorrow morning. I can prepare him and explain what to expect. And he’s an intelligent young man who has a great deal of respect for experience.

“In Rafael’s case, a connection we have with a commercial partner in Brazil – agency FWD – also played a crucial role; they are doing an excellent job with the Camara project. Everything fell into place perfectly.”

Preparing Camara for his F1 debut at the Brazilian GP required a specific approach. After a career built on chasing pole positions, race wins and championship titles, the rookie suddenly found himself in an environment where success is measured by entirely different criteria.

“Over the last week, we’ve had to reset everything,” Zanarini explained. “We’re with a team where – barring some extraordinary turn of events – we won’t be taking pole positions or winning races. Rafael is used to fighting for wins, so we’ve had to explain to him that the nature of the work is different now. If he does a good job, the time will come when he’ll have a car capable of securing pole positions and victories.”
Enrico Zanarini with Giancarlo Fisichella

For Zanarini, reaching F1 isn’t just the culmination of a journey; it’s the start of a new chapter. And when asked which of the drivers he has managed was most similar to Camara in terms of raw talent, his answer is telling: “Perhaps [Giancarlo] Fisichella. It’s very difficult to make comparisons, but in terms of pure talent, he’s the one who comes to mind. Their personalities, however, are completely different – one is introverted, the other extroverted.”

There is also an aspect of a manager’s job that rarely comes to light: managing the families. “We’ve practically earned a degree in ‘parent management’!” Zanarini exclaimed. “I think we deserve a special award. Sometimes, managing the parents is more demanding than managing the drivers. Families have sacrificed so much to help their children reach these levels, and the emotional bond is incredibly strong. But there comes a point when the young driver needs to become independent, and guiding that transition isn’t always easy.”
From Ron Dennis to Zak Brown, a less arrogant paddock
Zanarini experienced a version of F1 where decisions were made directly by team owners – a world where personal relationships were often decisive, albeit not always straightforward.

He recalls a meeting with Ron Dennis, arranged to discuss Giancarlo Fisichella following his victory at the 2003 Brazilian GP: “He received me in his hotel room, near Imola. He was arrogant right from the start. He told me he wasn’t interested in Fisichella and he had only agreed to meet me because I had asked him to. There are different ways to tell someone you’re not interested, and he certainly didn’t choose the most elegant one…”

The contrast with McLaren’s current leadership is stark: “Zak Brown has a very similar spirit to mine. I always say that I’m a used-car salesman, because that’s the industry I come from. And when you work in a showroom, you learn that you have to listen to everyone. Someone might walk in who looks like they don’t have a penny to their name, and then end up buying three Mercedes. Zak listens to everyone, and then, naturally, he draws his own conclusions.”

Paradoxically, even though F1 has become much more complex and affluent, it now strikes Zanarini as less arrogant than it used to be: “Back then, there were individual owners; today, the structures are different, and there is more dialogue. I don’t see the same kind of arrogance in today’s paddock that I sometimes encountered back then.”

Zanarini’s comparison between the Bernie Ecclestone era and the Liberty Media era is also devoid of nostalgia. While he acknowledges that the old system worked at the time, he believes the current management is far better-suited to the scale that F1 has reached.
Antonio Giovinazzi, Haas F1 Team and Enrico Zanarini
After 50 years in the business, Zanarini shows no signs of slowing down. When asked if he has ever considered leaving motorsport, his reply is immediate: “No – because the very next day, I’d die!”

Yet, there is an awareness that the future of the agency must eventually be entrusted to a new generation. This is where Francesco Principe enters the picture, having been given responsibility for the Camara project.

“This project is entirely in his hands, which gives me immense satisfaction,” Zanarini said. “Francesco Principe is, in a sense, my own creation – I say that with pride. We’ve developed a symbiosis where his fresh, youthful mindset complements my own experience.”

The bond goes beyond professional matters: “My own children chose different career paths. In the world of motorsport, Francesco is my son. I know that my own journey will come to an end one day, but it’s comforting to know that there will be someone to carry this work forward.”

Perhaps this passage best encapsulates the story of Enrico Zanarini – a man who has witnessed the evolution of race cars, teams, regulations, and the very way business is conducted in motorsport. He has known drivers who went on to win world championships, as well as others who saw their dreams vanish just meters into a qualifying lap.

And now, half a century later, he still finds himself reflected in those two words that once appeared on a television screen on a particularly bitter afternoon: “Try Harder.” Try again – and try better.

items.originalTitle: Las Vegas GP reveals neon-inspired trophy for 2026
detailZh: 拉斯维加斯大奖赛为2026年的F1赛事揭晓了一款新奖杯，其设计灵感来源于城市标志性的霓虹灯牌和复古照明招牌。
这款奖杯是自该赛事于2023年加入F1赛历以来使用的第二个设计，其独特的V型轮廓代表着拉斯维加斯和胜利。
然而，社交媒体上的粉丝迅速提出了V型设计的第三种含义：‘V代表维斯塔潘’，开玩笑说这个奖杯可能是为红牛车队的马克斯·维斯塔潘量身定做的。
其设计借鉴了与著名弗里蒙特街传统上相关的霓虹灯和白炽灯招牌，这个概念旨在让赛事获胜者拥有自己的照明拉斯维加斯标志。
冠军奖杯高22英寸，宽8¼英寸，重8磅（3.6千克），由实心复合材料制成，并镀有铜和铬。它还配备了122个独立灯光，并有一个五英尺的周界灯光。
该设计由拉斯维加斯大奖赛与Bowen Studios和Ore Designs合作开发。Bowen Studios负责奖杯的3D模型、渲染和动画，而Ore Designs，由Shane Larson领导，负责设计和制造实体奖杯。
Bowen Studios和Ore Designs之前曾合作开发了2023年至2025年的拉斯维加斯大奖赛奖杯，以及过去两年的美国大奖赛奖杯。
detailEn: The Las Vegas Grand Prix has unveiled a new trophy for its 2026 Formula 1 race, with a design inspired by the city's iconic neon signs and vintage illuminated marquees.
The trophy is the second design used since the event joined the F1 calendar in 2023 and features a distinctive V-shaped silhouette, representing both Vegas and victory.
However, fans on social media were quick to suggest a third meaning behind the V-shaped design: 'V for Verstappen', joking that the trophy could be tailor-made for Red Bull's Max Verstappen.

Its design draws on the neon and incandescent-bulb signage traditionally associated with the famous Fremont Street, with the concept intended to give the race winner their own illuminated Las Vegas sign.

The winner's trophy measures 22 inches high and 8¼ inches wide, weighs 8lbs (3.6kg) and is made from solid composite with copper and chrome plating. Alongside its 122 individual lights, it features a five-foot perimeter light.

The design was developed by the Las Vegas Grand Prix in collaboration with Bowen Studios and Ore Designs. Bowen Studios was responsible for the trophy's 3D model, renderings and animations, while Ore Designs, led by Shane Larson, engineered and fabricated the physical trophies.
Bowen Studios and Ore Designs previously worked together on the Las Vegas Grand Prix trophies from 2023 to 2025, as well as the past two United States Grand Prix trophies.

detailZh: 克里斯蒂安·霍纳揭示马克斯·维斯塔潘的管理团队如何改变了红牛2022年的研发方向
前红牛负责人克里斯蒂安·霍纳透露，马克斯·维斯塔潘的管理团队要求车队将2022年赛车研发方向从塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯身上转移开
马克斯·维斯塔潘、红牛车队、塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯、红牛车队
致红牛车迷。关注红牛车队，获取来自米尔顿凯恩斯的F1新闻、车手动态、技术洞察与比赛分析。
关于塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯在红牛车队效力期间的叙述，往往集中在他无法持续展现出与队友马克斯·维斯塔潘相同的原始速度上。但红牛车队前首席执行官兼领队克里斯蒂安·霍纳最近揭开了幕后工程之争的帷幕，这场争斗改变了佩雷斯2022赛季的轨迹。
霍纳在《高性能》播客中谈到他在米尔顿凯恩斯车队执掌二十年的经历时透露，2022年的初始底盘小红牛18并非天生按照维斯塔潘的极端偏好打造。相反，这辆早期地面效应赛车是2021年全年由当时的储备车手亚历克斯·阿尔本在模拟器中开发的，结果是一台更平衡、更可预测的机器。
“亚历克斯·阿尔本在幕后开发22款赛车方面做了了不起的工作……那非常符合他的驾驶风格，这是一种更经典的驾驶方式，可能更接近塞尔吉奥或丹尼尔（里卡多），”霍纳解释道。
由于2022年的初始赛车拥有可预测的车头，并且缺乏维斯塔潘偏好的那种极端、突然的旋转，佩雷斯一上来就表现出色。
霍纳指出：“当我们开始2022赛季时，如果你还记得，马克斯讨厌那辆车，车有太多转向不足，而塞尔吉奥凭借那种可预测性……突然间他们各自赢得了一场比赛，”他指的是年初两人激烈的竞争。
但内部均势是短暂的。意识到（当时的）卫冕世界冠军难以最大化一辆为传统驾驶风格调校的赛车，维斯塔潘的管理团队介入，迫使进行重大技术转向。
霍纳确认，在2022年阿塞拜疆大奖赛周末期间发生了一次直接对峙。
马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队，塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯，红牛车队
霍纳透露：“我记得那年阿塞拜疆站前后，我和马克斯的经纪团队坐下来谈，他们对我说：‘你看，你是围绕佩雷兹来开发这辆车的；你需要去顺应马克斯的需求。’”
面对这位当家车手阵营发出的最后通牒，红牛的工程部门决定调整研发方向。霍纳承认，车队优先考虑了这位“核心资产”的需求，因为维斯塔潘终究拥有更高的性能上限。
霍纳承认：“马克斯是核心资产，他是你最有希望用来赢下车手的车手……当然，任何工程团队都会自然而然地倾向于他们最快的车手。”
随着红牛对小红牛18进行研发，消除转向不足并引入更锐利、响应更灵敏的车头，维斯塔潘的速度爆发了。反过来，这条研发路径也剥夺了佩雷兹所习惯的可预测性，导致两位车手之间出现了巨大的性能差距。
detailEn: Christian Horner reveals how Max Verstappen’s management reshaped 2022 Red Bull development
Former Red Bull boss Christian Horner reveals Max Verstappen's management demanded the team shift its 2022 car development away from Sergio Perez
Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Sergio Perez, Red Bull Racing
For Red Bull fans. Keeping watch on Red Bull Racing, with F1 news, driver updates, technical insight and race analysis from Milton Keynes.

The narrative surrounding Sergio Perez's tenure at Red Bull Racing often centres on his inability to consistently extract the same raw pace as his team-mate Max Verstappen. But former Red Bull Racing CEO and team principal Christian Horner recently pulled back the curtain on a behind-the-scenes engineering battle that altered the trajectory of Perez's 2022 season.

Speaking on the High Performance podcast about his two-decade stint at the helm of the Milton Keynes squad, Horner revealed that the initial 2022 chassis, the RB18, was not inherently built to Verstappen's extreme preferences. Instead, the early ground-effect car was developed in the simulator by then-reserve driver Alex Albon throughout 2021, resulting in a more balanced, predictable machine.

"Alex Albon did a hell of a job in the background developing the '22 car... it was very much around his style of driving, which [is a] much more classic way of driving that was probably more akin to a Sergio or a Daniel [Ricciardo]," Horner explained.
Because the initial 2022 car possessed a predictable front end and lacked the extreme, snappy rotation that Verstappen prefers, Perez thrived right out of the gate.

"When we started the '22 season, if you remember that Max hated the car, it had too much understeer in the car, and Sergio with that predictability... suddenly they were winning a race apiece," Horner noted, referencing their close fight at the start of the year.

But the internal parity was short-lived. Recognising that the (then) reigning world champion was struggling to maximise a car geared toward a traditional driving style, Verstappen's management team stepped in to force a major technical pivot.
Horner confirmed that a direct confrontation occurred during the 2022 Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend.
Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Sergio Perez, Red Bull Racing
"I remember sitting down with Max's management around Azerbaijan that year and them saying, 'Look, you've developed this car around Checo; you need to be following what Max needs,'" Horner revealed.

Faced with an ultimatum from the camp of its franchise driver, Red Bull's engineering department made the decision to shift its development path. Horner admitted that the team prioritised the demands of its "prime asset" because Verstappen ultimately possessed the higher performance ceiling.
"Max is the prime asset, he's the driver you're most likely going to win with... of course any engineering team will gravitate just naturally towards their fastest driver," Horner admitted.

As Red Bull developed the RB18 to strip away the understeer and introduce a sharper, more responsive front end, Verstappen's pace exploded. Conversely, the development path stripped away the predictability that Perez was used to, leading to a massive performance delta between the two drivers.

detailZh: 詹姆斯·阿利森透露梅赛德斯四年F1冠军荒期间对新员工的寄语
阿利森告诉数百名新员工，他们终将赢得比赛，并把世界冠军收入囊中
致梅赛德斯车迷。关于银箭车队的最新消息，包括来自布拉克利和布里克斯沃思的F1新闻、车手动态、赛车研发和比赛分析。
梅赛德斯技术总监詹姆斯·阿利森透露，在车队成绩低迷的几年里，他曾告诉数百名加入布拉克利车队的员工，他们终将赢得比赛，并夺得属于自己的世界冠军。
梅赛德斯在2014年至2021年间连续八次赢得车队总冠军，但随后四个赛季无缘冠军，直到2026年才重新包揽两项桂冠，基米·安东内利在墨西哥大奖赛成为最年轻的世界冠军，而车队一周后在巴西大奖赛锁定车队总冠军。
阿利森在NU银箭电台节目中表示，他在2023年注意到，许多自车队上次夺冠以来加入的人感到运气不佳。
“我感觉到，2021年之后、也就是我们上一次夺冠之后加入车队的约400人，看起来有点自怜，他们加入时以为是一支常胜之师，结果发现自己来得正是时候不巧，”这位英国人解释道。
随后，他在面向全厂的讲话中直接对这群人说了话。
“你们不是运气不好；你们是这家工厂里最幸运的人，因为我们将再次获胜，”他告诉他们。“而且你们知道，当我们做到时，你们全程都在那里。这不是你们蹭来的别人的冠军——是你们亲手打造的。你们将永远能够称它为你们自己的。这是你们的派对。”
乔治·拉塞尔，梅赛德斯；安德烈亚·基米·安东内利，梅赛德斯
艾利森表示，该群体此后已增长到“600人以上”，并认为因此这个冠军对他们来说意义更加重大。
“那些人知道，这个冠军是他们从一开始就在场并亲手造就的。那是一种特别强烈的感受，”他补充道。
艾利森强调，这一成功在很大程度上要归功于那些从不去比赛现场的员工。他表示，梅赛德斯在其布拉克利底盘基地和布里克斯沃思引擎工厂共有“约2000名”员工。
他解释道：“车队中约有8%的人参与外出比赛，而让这一切成为可能、创造圈速并交付所有这些成果、使我们最前端的车手能够真正加以利用的绝大部分工作，都发生在这座工厂里。”
detailEn: James Allison reveals message to Mercedes recruits during team's four-year F1 title drought
Allison told hundreds of new employees they would eventually win and claim the championship as their own
For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth.

Mercedes technical director James Allison has revealed how he told hundreds of staff members who joined the Brackley outfit during the team's lean years that they would one day win, and that the championship would be theirs.

Mercedes won eight consecutive constructors' titles between 2014 and 2021, but then went four seasons without a championship before claiming both crowns in 2026, with Kimi Antonelli becoming the youngest champion at the Mexican Grand Prix and the team securing the constructors' crown at the Brazilian Grand Prix a week later.
Speaking on the NU Silver Arrows Radio Show, Allison said he noticed in 2023 that many of the people who had joined since the team's last title were feeling unlucky.

"I got a sense that the 400 or so people who joined the team after 2021, the last time previously we'd won, were looking a bit sorry for themselves, having joined what they thought was a winning juggernaut, only to find that they'd arrived at just the wrong moment," the Briton explained.
He then addressed that group directly in a talk to the whole factory.

"You are not unlucky; you're the luckiest people in this factory, because we are going to win again," he told them. "And you know that when we do, you were there for the whole of that. It isn't someone else's championship that you've glommed on to - you built it. And you'll always be able to call it your own. It's your party."
George Russell, Mercedes, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes
Allison said that group has since grown to "something upwards of 600" people, and believes the title means even more to them as a result.
"Those people know that this championship is something that they were there for from the start and made their own. And that is a particularly powerful feeling," he added.
Allison was keen to stress how much of the success is down to staff who never go to races. He said Mercedes has "about 2,000" people across its Brackley chassis base and Brixworth engine factory.

"About 8% of the team do the travelling part, and the vast majority of what makes it all possible - what creates the lap time and delivers all this stuff so that the tip of our spear can actually use it - is back here in the factory," he explained.

detailZh: 哈斯车队决定在拉斯维加斯站继续留用拉斐尔·卡马拉
新手车手卡马拉将获得另一个机会为2027年的完整F1首秀做准备
拉斐尔·卡马拉将在即将到来的拉斯维加斯大奖赛中再次为哈斯车队参赛，而平田翔太将取代奥利·贝尔曼在首场练习赛中的位置
在墨西哥城大奖赛周末期间被解雇的埃斯特班·奥康被解雇后，平田翔太和卡马拉都已为车队参赛
Hirakawa在摩纳哥参加世界耐力锦标赛决赛——后来赢得了他的第三个WEC冠军——因此无法参加之前在巴西的F1赛事，这给了哈斯车队一个机会，让Camara提前亮相。
Camara将留在赛车中参加拉斯维加斯的比赛，为他为车队在下一赛季的全职F1首秀积累宝贵经验。与此同时，贝尔曼今年至今只为一个FP1赛段让出了座位，因此他将最后一次让出座位，以便给Hirakawa在VF-26赛车中获得更多赛道时间。
Hirakawa在墨西哥城的F1首秀中获得了积分，尽管在奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里和两位阿尔卑斯车手被处以赛后罚分之后，他给车队总监小松洋雄留下了“非常好的心理素质——[他]非常干净。他做到了我们期望的。”的印象。
Camara的处子秀更加艰难，因为圣保罗赛道（Interlagos）的天气条件极其多变。这位巴西人在周末逐渐提升状态，FP3结束时展现出了良好的速度，但雨在排位赛之前到来，使他的生活变得更加困难。
在Q1从打滑中挽救了自己的赛车后，卡马拉进入了Q2，但在12号弯道由于在低抓地力条件下无法正确调整后轴制动，导致赛车撞上了墙壁。
因此，他获得了第13个发车位，但由于其他车手受到发车位处罚，他实际上从第11位起步，但在中雨轮胎的艰难比赛中，卡马拉几乎掉到了车队的最后。
鉴于卡马拉在F2车手积分榜上的位置，他是否会留在车队参加剩余赛季还不确定；他可能希望完成本赛季，但这将很大程度上取决于哈斯车队和法拉利的决定。
如果卡马拉决定参加卡塔尔和阿布扎比的赛事，那么伊拉卡瓦可以在这些比赛中重返赛车。
detailEn: Haas sticks with Rafael Camara for Las Vegas, Ryo Hirakawa in for FP1
Rookie driver Camara gets another chance to prepare for his full F1 debut in 2027
Rafael Camara will race again for Haas at Formula 1's upcoming Las Vegas Grand Prix, as Ryo Hirakawa takes Ollie Bearman's seat for the opening practice session.
Both Hirakawa and Camara have now raced for the team following the dismissal of Esteban Ocon, who was stood down during the Mexico City Grand Prix weekend.

Hirakawa, contesting the World Endurance Championship finale in Monza - later winning his third WEC title - was unavailable for the previous F1 round in Brazil and this presented Haas an opportunity to bring Camara in for an early debut.

Camara will stay in the car for Las Vegas, as he gathers valuable experience for his full F1 debut next season with the team. Bearman meanwhile has only given up his seat for one FP1 session so far this year, so will do so for the final time to present Hirakawa with more track time in the VF-26.

Hirakawa scored a point in his Mexico City F1 debut, albeit after Oscar Piastri and the two Alpine drivers were handed post-race penalties, and impressed team principal Ayao Komatsu with "very good mental conviction - [he was] so clean. He delivered what we expected."

Camara endured a tougher debut run, as conditions at Interlagos were incredibly variable. The Brazilian built up through the weekend and showed good pace by the end of FP3, but the rain arrived ahead of qualifying and made his life more difficult.
After rescuing his car from a spin in Q1, Camara got as far as Q2 - but put his car into the wall at Turn 12 having been unable to get the correct rear-axle braking in low-grip conditions.
He thus qualified 13th and started 11th with other drivers taking grid penalties, but a tough stint on the intermediates put Camara towards the back of the field.

It is uncertain whether Camara will stay in the car for the rest of the season, given his position at the top of the F2 drivers' standings; he may wish to complete the season, but this will largely be at the behest of Haas and Ferrari.
Hirakawa could feasibly return to the car in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, should Camara return to F2 for those rounds.

items.titleZh: 哈斯确认卡马拉出战拉斯维加斯站
items.summaryZh: 哈斯车队宣布，新签下的拉斐尔·卡马拉将在拉斯维加斯大奖赛继续驾驶赛车，此前他在巴西完成了混乱的F1首秀。
items.originalTitle: Vegas gives Camara chance to put messy debut behind him
items.summaryEn: Haas has announced that new signing Rafael Camara will stay in the car for the Las Vegas Grand Prix, following his messy Formula 1 debut in Brazil.
detailZh: 哈斯新签下的拉斐尔·卡马拉将很快获得机会，摆脱他在巴西混乱的F1首秀，因为他将继续驾驶赛车出战本周末的拉斯维加斯大奖赛。
卡马拉的首秀因哈斯与埃斯特班·奥康戏剧性且突然的分手而从2027年提前，但最初的公告只确认卡马拉出战英特拉格斯。
如今哈斯宣布他将继续留在拉斯维加斯站，而曾在墨西哥大奖赛周末中途顶替奥康的平川亮，将回到阵容中，在第一次自由练习中驾驶奥利·贝尔曼的赛车。
不过拉斯维加斯之后的情况可能更复杂，因为F1最后几站卡塔尔和阿布扎比同期也有F2比赛，而卡马拉目前以仅7分的优势领跑F2积分榜，领先红牛储备车手尼科拉·措洛夫。鉴于赛程安排，同一周末同时参加F2和F1实际上是不可能的。
卡马拉表示，他“期待在拉斯维加斯重新坐进赛车”，因为巴西站是一次“很好的学习经历”。
车队领队小松礼雄表示，卡马拉的首秀是在“极具挑战性的条件下”完成的，但他仍然“向我们和全世界展示了他为什么值得我们签下他，直到2027年”。
卡马拉在那场首秀周末中排名第20位，也就是最后一名，落后两圈。但考虑到在那场比赛之前他从未驾驶过2026年的哈斯赛车，再加上不断变化的天气条件，他面临着许多可以理解的不利因素。
就首秀周末而言，很难想象还有比拉斐尔·卡马拉所面对的更为艰难的处境了。
他直到本周初才被临时召入，此前从未驾驶过哈斯赛车或任何2026款F1赛车。这压力巨大且充满挑战，而天气预报也从未显示出对他有利的迹象。事实证明果然如此。
同样令人沮丧和鼓舞的是，卡马拉展现出了许多潜力的闪光点。他在排位赛中非常快，并让自己处于一个非常有利的位置，即便排位赛期间下了雨。如果他在艰难条件下首秀就闯入Q3，那也不会令人意外，那将是非常令人印象深刻的表现。
在大奖赛的干胎阶段，他与队友奥利·贝尔曼相比实际上表现不错：在两段软胎 阶段中平均每圈慢约十分之一秒。但需要注意的是，贝尔曼的比赛受到了影响，他有一段时间陷入了车流。卡马拉在比赛开始和结束时使用半雨胎的阶段特别弱：与软胎相比，这两段与贝尔曼的差距都大幅扩大。
他在排位赛中的两次失误无疑让他的信心受到了一些打击。第一次是水滑和车轮打滑的混合作用，导致赛车在雷塔奥波斯塔直道上失控甩尾。第二次是在12号弯洪考弯锁死轮胎——许多车手在那里都遇到了麻烦——随后相当猛烈地撞上了护栏。
他在比赛开始时没有过度推进是可以理解的。事实上，哈斯车队很可能鼓励他不要冒任何愚蠢的风险。因此他花了一段时间才慢慢进入状态并找到节奏，但当他找到节奏时，他的速度非常非常快。
如果他在最后阶段能有一段更强的中途跑（inter stint）会更好。但到那时已经没有什么可争取的了，他只需要把车安全带回，所以这一点可以理解。
在获得第20名、落后两圈完赛后，他的F1生涯只会从这里变得更好。这不仅仅是因为成绩在纸面上如此糟糕，还因为他在排位赛和大奖赛中展现出的真正潜力也时有闪现。
detailEn: Haas's new signing Rafael Camara will get a quick chance to move on from his messy Formula 1 debut in Brazil as he will stay in the car for this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix.
Camara's debut was brought forward from 2027 following Haas's dramatic and abrupt split with Esteban Ocon, but the original announcement only committed to Camara racing at Interlagos.
Now Haas has announced he will stay on for Vegas, with Ryo Hirakawa - who initially jumped in for Ocon mid-way through the Mexican GP weekend - back in the line-up for FP1 in Ollie Bearman's car.

The situation beyond Vegas may be more complicated though, as the final F1 rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi also have Formula 2 on the bill, and Camara currently leads the F2 standings by just seven points over Red Bull reserve Nikola Tsolov. It is effectively impossible to race in both F2 and F1 over the same weekend given the schedules.
Camara said he was "looking forward to getting back in the car in Las Vegas" as Brazil had been a "good learning experience".
Team principal Ayao Komatsu said Camara's debut had been in "extremely challenging conditions" but that he's still "showed us and the world why we signed him for 2027".

Camara ended that debut weekend 20th and last, two laps down. But having never driven the 2026 Haas before that event, and given the changing weather conditions, he faced plenty of mitigating factors.
As debut weekends go, it's hard to imagine tougher circumstances than the ones Rafael Camara faced.

He only got called up at the start of the week and hadn't driven the Haas or any 2026 F1 car before. This was high pressure and challenging, and the forecast never looked like it was going to be on his side. And so it proved.

What's probably equally frustrating and encouraging is that there were so many flashes of potential from Camara. He was very quick in qualifying and got himself into a really nice place, even with the rain that fell during the session. It would not have been a surprise if he'd snuck into Q3 on debut in tough conditions, which would have been very impressive.

In the slick running in the grand prix, he actually compared well to team-mate Ollie Bearman: about a tenth of a second a lap slower on average across two stints on softs. The caveat is that Bearman's race was compromised and he spent some time in traffic. Camara was particularly weak in the intermediate running at the start of the race and again at the end: the gap to Bearman ballooned in both of those stints compared with the softs.

His confidence was surely battered a little by his two offs in qualifying. The first was a mix of aquaplaning and wheelspin that sent the car fishtailing out of control down the Reta Oposta straight. The second was a lock-up at the Juncao Turn 12, where a lot of drivers had trouble, followed by a fairly heavy hit into the barrier.

You can forgive him for not over-pushing at the start of the race. In fact, Haas probably encouraged him not to take any silly risks. So it took a while for him to ease his way in and find his rhythm but, when he did, he was very, very quick.
It would have been better if he could have had a stronger inter stint at the end. But by that point there was nothing to play for and he just needed to bring it home, so you can understand that.

After finishing 20th and two laps down, his F1 career will only get better from here. That's not just because the result was so weak on paper but because the glimpses of his true potential throughout qualifying and the grand prix were there too.
